headline: Rate Worries and Hormuz Tension Frame Friday's Open After a Broad Thursday Retreat
body_html:
U.S. stocks open Friday after a lopsided Thursday, November 12, session in which 489 of the 668 stocks we track fell and only 175 rose. Homebuilders lost 2.68% and consumer names 2.1%. Energy was the only sector group to finish higher, up 0.1%. Early prices carry little meaning, so the tone set overnight matters more.

Currency and rate markets lean cautious. The dollar sits near a 19-month high as traders bet on a Fed rate hike, and the yen is testing the 160 level. India's rupee slipped as oil and U.S. yields weighed on local stocks and bonds. Crude is on course for a second weekly decline, with Washington holding its blockade of Iran. Fresh Gulf incidents, including a reported mine strike on an LNG tanker in Hormuz, keep the risk premium alive.

At the open, watch whether tech can hold its recent strength. AMD rose 5.86% and HubSpot 6.39% on Thursday, while Corteva sank 24.3%. Cisco's earnings beat and its forecast that AI infrastructure revenue will double this fiscal year should shape sentiment in networking and chips, and the rate and dollar backdrop could cap any bounce.

briefs.headline: Gulf Incidents Keep Shipping on Edge
briefs.body: Iran said an LNG tanker struck a mine and suffered an explosion in the Strait of Hormuz. Separately, Iran's Guards claimed they targeted a U.S. early-warning radar in Bahrain. Traders will watch for any spillover into energy and shipping at the open.

briefs.headline: Dollar Firm on Fed Hike Bets, Yen Under Pressure
briefs.body: The dollar hovers near a 19-month high as markets price in a possible Fed rate hike. The yen is testing the 160 mark, a level that often draws attention from officials. Higher U.S. yields are also weighing on emerging-market currencies such as the rupee.

briefs.headline: Oil Eyes Second Weekly Loss Despite Pipeline Attack Claim
briefs.body: Crude is set for a second straight weekly decline as the U.S. sticks with its blockade of Iran. Yemen's Houthis, however, said they attacked a pumping station on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline. Energy was Thursday's lone gaining sector, up 0.1%.

briefs.headline: Cisco Beat Puts AI Networking Back in Focus
briefs.body: Cisco topped earnings expectations and said its AI infrastructure revenue should double this fiscal year. The upbeat outlook could lift networking and semiconductor names. Semiconductors fell 0.83% on Thursday, though AMD climbed 5.86%.

briefs.headline: Cerebras Jumps on Revenue Beat and Microsoft Deal
briefs.body: Cerebras surged about 13% after reporting quarterly revenue above forecasts and announcing a deal with Microsoft. The move adds to enthusiasm around AI hardware challengers. Investors will gauge whether the momentum spreads to peers at the open.

briefs.headline: Corteva Leads a Rough Day for Decliners
briefs.body: Corteva dropped 24.3% on Thursday, the steepest fall in our universe. Cellebrite lost 14.25%, Digi International 12.72%, Warby Parker 11.34% and YETI 10.49%. Consumer names were hit hard, and the sector fell 2.1%.
